prompt: You are the test author this time: write isCorrect so it accepts a correct WordCounter and rejects broken ones. Complete the checker in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Three separate contract promises are invisible to a single call with a well-behaved list. Case-insensitivity only shows when the same word arrives in two capitalisations; the difference between counting and merely recording only shows when a word appears twice; and "an empty list gives an empty map, never null" can only be checked by passing an empty list. The destructive implementation is the subtle one -- it returns exactly the right map, and the only evidence is the caller's own list afterwards, which is why the checker must pass a MUTABLE list (List.of is immutable and would make that bug throw instead of showing itself).
hints: Use a list where one word appears twice in different capitalisations, such as ["Cat", "dog", "cat"], and check the count is 2.
Call it with an empty list and check you get back an empty map rather than null -- getting null back and calling .size() on it is itself a crash.
Pass a mutable list (new ArrayList<>(...)) and check afterwards that it still has its elements: one implementation consumes what you give it.
